title: Full-round AES-192 chosen-key limited-birthday distinguisher, DGLP 2025

target.description: Full 12-round AES-192 with the standard key schedule, initial AddRoundKey, and no final MixColumns; Section 2.1 and Figure 6/Table 3.

setting.reference_model: Source Definition 2 and Theorem 1 use a limited-birthday relation and a generic black-box 128-bit permutation with forward and inverse access. Section 4.2.1 uses source dimensions din=7 and dout=14 and reports max(2^((129-max(7,14))/2),2^(129-(7+14))) = 2^108 encryption queries to construct one acceptable pair.
setting.key_relation: Attacker constructs (K,K XOR DeltaK) conforming to the entire Table 3 standard key-schedule characteristic; DeltaK = 2D3D06BB 0C000000 3D9D9DBC 00000000 0C000000 2D9D9DBC, obtained from the first six master-key words in Tables 3-4. This is chosen-key construction, not a related-secret-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Attacker-selected XOR-related key pairs satisfying the stated full key-schedule characteristic; not arbitrary unknown keys.
setting.plaintext_model: Two attacker-constructed, generally distinct inputs P,P' satisfying the prescribed input-difference set, with AES-192_K(P) XOR AES-192_{K XOR DeltaK}(P') in the prescribed output-difference set.
assumptions: Chosen-key/open-key limited-birthday witness construction under Section 2.3 Definition 2; not the ordinary single-secret-key PRP game and not key recovery.
The standard AES key schedule is respected; the keys and internal starting points are deliberately constructed to satisfy the trail.
The ideal-case figures are the authors' relation-specific comparison, not interchangeable with exhaustive secret-key search.
The attacker generates 2^61 conforming key pairs for the inbound search. This is not a secret-key-oracle count; no distinct-key total or pair-overlap count is reported.

time.note: Section 4.2.1 includes generation of 2^61 conforming key pairs at 2^28 work per pair (2^89 total), plus 2^39 inbound starting points per key pair and 2^100 outbound trials. Table 1 reports 2^100. The paper does not provide a full-encryption conversion for all rebound/key-generation operations. The supply of 2^61 conforming key pairs remains an evidence task; see coverage issue dglp2025-aes192-key-pair-supply.

data.note: No independent external-oracle data budget is given for this offline chosen-key construction. Inbound starting-point counts and generated key pairs are not silently relabeled as chosen-plaintext queries.

memory.note: Table 1 and Section 4.2.1 report 2^32 memory for Super-Sbox lookup storage. Entry size is not normalized to bytes or 128-bit blocks.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing budget is reported. Attack-specific conforming-key generation costs 2^89 and is included in total time; Section 4.2.1 Step 3 builds 2^32-value Super-Sbox tables for selected differences and keys.

success.description: Section4.2.1 prices an expected single chosen-key limited-birthday witness, with2^61 conforming key pairs and2^39 inbound starting points each. The source states conditional outbound and key-characteristic probabilities, but no numerical probability of finding at least one witness at that finite budget. Section2.6 explicitly uses1/p for an expected event, not an independently repeated-trial success formula.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit of defining construction and parameter passages, not a new full-paper or forward-literature audit. Source local/conditional models, expected counts, key-relation construction and full recovery remain separate.

PDF16: rounds4–10 contribute2^-72 to the conditional outbound characteristic.
PDF16: the round1 active S-boxes contribute2^-28 to the conditional outbound characteristic.

PDF16: after fixing16 of20 active key S-boxes, four residual transitions each have source probability2^-7. This2^-28 is the local remaining test in the chosen-key construction, distinct from the unrestricted2^-135 key characteristic.

The source states conditional outbound and key-characteristic probabilities, but no numerical probability of finding at least one witness at that finite budget. limitations: The claim is a chosen-key distinguisher and does not recover a secret AES key or establish a single-secret-key attack.
No numerical end-to-end success probability, standalone oracle-data budget, or separately reusable preprocessing cost is supplied.
The reported attack work and Super-Sbox-entry memory remain native units; no normalization unsupported by the source was made.

Section 4.2.1 reports a key-characteristic probability of 2^-135 and requires 2^61 conforming pairs. Interpreting that probability as an exact fraction of all 192-bit keys for fixed DeltaK would suggest 2^57 pairs. Whether the probability is only a local S-box-product estimate or the construction ranges over a larger difference/counting domain remains to be explained; no corrected attack exponent is inferred.
